approachQuestion.prompt:
Steady Supports. Return whether a binary support tree is steady: at every node, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most one. An absent subtree has height 0; a non-empty subtree has height one plus its larger child height. An empty tree is steady.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 1(2(4(-,-),-),3(-,-)). Output: true. Example 2: Input: 1(2(4(6(-,-),-),-),3(-,5(-,7(-,-)))). Output: false: the root has equally tall children, but node 2 is unsteady. Example 3: Input: -. Output: true.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; labels are arbitrary signed 32-bit integers and irrelevant. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes. Shape is unrestricted. Return only a Boolean.

options.text: Use explicit postorder frames to return a subtree height and whether it is steady. Combine both child flags and check their height difference at the current node.
options.feedback: The returned flag carries failures from any depth, while child heights check the current node.

options.text: At every node separately traverse both child subtrees to measure heights and check the difference. Return true only if every such test passes.
options.feedback: This checks the complete definition correctly, but height scans overlap. Passing heights upward once removes the repeated work.

options.text: Measure the two root-child heights and return whether their difference is at most one.
options.feedback: Example 2 passes the root test but fails at node 2. The property is required everywhere.

options.text: Return true only when every leaf is at the same depth.
options.feedback: Example 1 is steady but has leaves at depths 1 and 2. Equal leaf depths are not required.

feedback.reason: Validate a local height condition at every subtree, not only at the root.
details: Use postorder frames, treating a missing child as height 0 and steady=true. After both children finish, return height 1+max(leftHeight,rightHeight) and a flag requiring both child flags and a height difference at most one. Process all nodes and return the root flag, or true for an empty tree.

The height difference rule must hold in every subtree, not only at the root. Combine both child validity flags with their heights. Computing heights afresh at each node would repeat completed subtree work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed postorder summary method consider n >= 1 nodes and height h in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case pair. Count active frames and their fixed-size heights/flags; exclude the supplied tree and Boolean output. No subtree heights are recomputed or stored after their parent consumes them.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: One postorder height/validity combine per node avoids repeated height scans.
details: Every node has one constant-time combine after its children. At most h fixed-size ancestor frames remain live; a chain attains that height.
By induction a returned flag is true precisely when all nodes in that subtree satisfy the height condition. Combining both child flags with the local height comparison proves the root result.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Every node has one constant-time combine after its children. At most h fixed-size ancestor frames remain live; a chain attains that height.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
